reading.body:
E-Foam in Winter Garden, Florida is tagged as a data center in this database, but that tag almost certainly reflects a mapping error rather than actual data center operations.

The facility name indicates foam fabrication or packaging materials manufacturing. Light industrial buildings on streets like Susan B. Britt Court typically house small manufacturing or distribution operations, not colocation facilities. A foam manufacturer may run ordinary office computers and an internal server closet, which serves the business itself but is functionally different from a data center that leases power and rack space to external tenants. No operator website, press mention, business registration, or independent documentation could confirm data center or hosting services at this address. Research attempts exhausted available public channels without finding any IT or telecommunications association for the name E-Foam.

The entry publishes no power capacity, operator specifications, or certifications. Without these basic markers, the facility cannot be read as evidence of AI infrastructure contribution. The database's ranking of E-Foam as the fifth-largest facility in Florida by published megawatts reflects only that it publishes nothing, not that it operates at scale. The classification should be treated as unverified until independent sources document actual data center use.
